intent: Make the session-autopsy surfacing honest and the compiled scripts reachable without Claude. The statusline badge counted all 182 candidates (nobody reviews 182 weak n-grams), and the compiled scripts had no zero-token entry point, so the deterministic 90% of each workflow still implied opening a Claude session.
scope: docs/explanations/ (new explanation doc + refreshed index, via the newly compiled explain_diff.sh scaffold)
Non-goal: changing detector rankings or REPORT.md content; only what the badge counts.
changes: state.json's unreviewed_count now counts only candidates with >=100k estimated weekly tokens (SIGNIFICANT_WEEKLY_TOKENS), so the badge went from a meaningless 182 to 7 items actually worth attention; the SessionStart one-liner and statusline badge inherit it for free since both read state.json.
report --mark-reviewed marks the same significant set, keeping dismiss/appear symmetric.
token-savers.zsh adds finish-gate / phone-deploy / autopsy / yay-clean shell functions so the deterministic halves run at zero LLM tokens; Claude enters only on failure triage.

verification.evidence: 81 passed; test_render_and_write_report now asserts unreviewed==1 with a mixed significant/insignificant corpus.

verification.command: PYTHONPATH=~/testsAndMisc python3 -m python_pkg.session_autopsy report; jq .unreviewed_count ~/.claude/autopsy/state.json; statusline.sh pipe-test
verification.evidence: unreviewed_count 182 -> 7 on the real corpus; statusline renders '[Fable] ~ | ⚙7'.
Both functions execute the real scripts from a fresh zsh; shellcheck -s bash clean after adding '; }' brace style.

risks: The 100k threshold is a judgment constant; a genuinely useful small candidate stays out of the badge (it remains in REPORT.md and candidates --json).
Shell functions shadow no existing commands today; a future binary named 'autopsy' or 'phone-deploy' on PATH would be shadowed by these functions in interactive shells.
rollback: Revert the three python files to restore all-candidates counting; delete linux_configuration/zsh/token-savers.zsh and the ~/.oh-my-zsh/custom symlink.
After rollback, 'autopsy report' stops resolving and state.json returns to counting every candidate.
